notes: §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.3.1 SR2 names the second type of required word: "Special character words. These are the arithmetic operators and relation characters." That is the ten the list at §1985:IV.8 ends with: the arithmetic operators of §1985:III.2 ("A single character or fixed two-character combination which belongs to the following set": + - * / **) and > < = >= <=. The lexer makes each one token and the expression grammar reads them where the formats print them (addOp, mulOp, powerExpression and unaryExpression for the binary and unary arithmetic operators; comparisonOperator for the relation characters with IS and NOT, where NOT stands only before =, > and <, as the 1985 relational operators do); none of these rules has an edition arm, so 85 reaches them as every edition does. The special character words a later edition added are each refused at 85 by an introduction gate: <> by RelationalOperatorGate.Check (called from VisitComparisonOperator) with COBOL0900, & by VisitConcatenationExpression, :: by VisitInlineMethodInvocation, *> by OnFloatingComment and a >> directive by its own COBOL0900. Probed at --std 85: all ten compile and compute as written in COMPUTE, IF, EVALUATE and PERFORM UNTIL, unary + and - included; <>, &, ::, *> and >>SOURCE each draw COBOL0900; NOT >=, NOT <=, == and the spaced forms "> =" and "* *" are syntax errors. The witness runs + - * / ** in one COMPUTE and >, = and < in three IF statements.

next.reason: 1985: "Special character words. These are the arithmetic operators and relation characters."; 2023: "| & | Concatenation operator | ... | == | Pseudo-text delimiter in COPY and REPLACE statements | ... | *> | ... | :: |". 2023 lists more special character words than arithmetic operators and relation characters: &, ==, *>, >> and ::, and = also serves as the COMPUTE assignment.
